resources.string: Use your location in the background?
Robo-Bike collects your phone’s location also when the app is closed or not in use, while your bike is connected and right after you switch it off. It uses it to:
record the route of each ride in your ride log
remember where you parked (“Where is my bike?”)
count the distance since you left home and warn you when the battery may not get you back
switch the light by sunrise, sunset and rain
Your location stays on your phone. Only for the rain check, a position rounded to about 1 km goes to the weather service Open-Meteo. No ads, no analytics.
This is optional. Without it, these features only work when you open the app before riding.
Next, Android asks for the permission.
To show turn arrows and distances on the display, Robo-Bike reads the navigation notification of Google Maps while you navigate.
It ignores all other notifications, such as messages, calls or other apps.
Nothing leaves your phone. The directions only go to your bike’s display over Bluetooth and into the app’s own diagnostics log, which you share only if you choose to.
This is optional: everything else works without it.
Next, Android opens its notification access settings: turn on Robo-Bike there.
